newsitem.title: CHINA: More than 400 million Chinese suffer low iodine.
newsitem.headline: More than 400 million Chinese suffer low iodine.

text.p: At least 400 million Chinese are suffering from iodine deficiency caused in part by consumption of low quality table salt, the China Daily said on Monday.

China would begin licensing salt producers, transporters and wholesalers as part of a drive to eliminate diseases caused by iodine deficiency by 2000, the newspaper quoted an official with industry regulator China National Salt Industry Corp as saying.
"It's known that at least 400 million Chinese suffer from iodine deficiency," the newspaper said.
Consumers were being urged not to buy salt from private producers, many of whom had cut costs and prices by not adding iodine, the official was quoted as saying.
About 25 percent of the eight million tonnes of edible salt sold in China last year was sold by private producers and did not have state-mandated levels of iodine, the official said.
China had spent nearly 1.0 billion yuan ($120 million) to combat iodine deficiency and had received $27 million in World Bank loans this year to promote the use of iodised salt, he said.
Consumption of iodised salt is the main intake of iodine for many rural and inland Chinese whose diets often do not contain other sources of iodine.
A shortage of iodine in the diet can cause goitre and brain damage and stunt the growth of children.
